question: Shellfishing in Galicia had a terrible year in 2023, and it was particularly bad in the Muros-Noia estuary, where even hatchlings are dying, leaving shellfish farmers without work for months.

However, they are prevented from applying for financial support under the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) in these circumstances as one of the funding requirements is that they must have carried out fishing activities for at least 120 days during the last two years. Indeed, that requirement prevents EMFAF aid from being of any use to the sector at a time when it needs it most. 1.
Is the Commission aware of this situation?

Does the Commission intend to amend the EMFF Regulation, which in Articles 33 and 34 establishes financial support for temporary and permanent cessation of activities, among other things, with a view to ensuring that those who have not been able to work the adequate number of days can benefit from the aid and that the aid is effective for those who need it most?
What alternatives does the Commission offer those working in the sector who currently have no form of income?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.2.2024) 1. The Commission is aware of the situation of the Galician shellfish sector and its socioeconomic concerns, through its dialogue with the Spanish national authorities. 2. Support from the European Maritime and Fisheries Fund (EMFF 2014-2020) is no longer available as the eligibility period for supported operations ended on 31 December 2023.

However, support for the temporary cessation of fishing activities is available from the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF 2021-2027). In their capacity as fishers on foot, shellfish gatherers are also eligible for this type of support1 which can be granted provided this measure is included in a Member State’s program under the EMFAF and a set of specific conditions are fulfilled.

At this point in time, there is no plan to modify the eligibility conditions set out in the EMFAF Regulation for this type of support. 3. In line with recital 32 of the EMFAF Regulation, EMFAF can support actions like mutual funds, insurance instruments or other collective schemes, which enhance the capacity of the sector to manage risks and respond to adverse events.

EMFAF can also support projects on the diversification of activities within or outside fisheries sector. Besides support from the EMFAF, the Member State can support shellfish gatherers with State aid and under the de minimis Regulation2.
1 In accordance with Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2021/1139 of the European Parliament and of the Council of
7 July 2021 establishing the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/1004 (OJ L 247, 13.7.2021, p. 1).

2 Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/2391 of 4 October 2023 amending Regulations (EU) No 717/2014, (EU) No 1407/2013, (EU) No 1408/2013 and (EU) No 360/2012 as regards de minimis aid for the processing and marketing of fishery and aquaculture products, and Regulation (EU) No 717/2014 as regards the total amount of de minimis aid granted to a single undertaking, its period of application and other matters.
